question.leadin: The man who assassinated this president bought an ivory-handled revolver for it because he thought it would look better in a museum.
question.text: Name this president who was shot by Charles Guiteau, a man who was bitter about not receiving a lucrative government job.
question.clue: This man defeated Winfield Scott Hancock to become president, and the Pendleton Civil Service Act was passed after his death.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about U.S. government relations with Native Americans in the late 19th century.
swap.text: At this 1876 battle, George Custer's 7th Cavalry Regiment was annihilated by the forces of Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse.
swap.clue: Recounts of this battle often feature the Lone Teepee, and leaders on one side were Frederick Benteen and Marcus Reno.

question.text: The Tenure of Office Act also prevented President Hayes from firing this man, who earned his job from Roscoe Conkling via the patronage system. As President, this successor of James Garfield would pass the Pendleton Act to end patronage.
question.clue: This president signed a compromise tariff that raised some duties and lowered others, leading it to be known as the "Mongrel Tariff."

swap.leadin: Eugene Debs was arrested in the aftermath of this event, after which he became a Socialist.
swap.text: Name this railroad strike and boycott that crippled transportation in 1894.
swap.clue: Mediation offers by the local Civic Federation and Mayor John P. Hopkins were turned down, and violence soon broke out at Blue Island.

question.text: As Ambassador to France, Franklin helped to negotiate this 1783 treaty which ended the American Revolution.
question.clue: Two years afer this treaty, it was clarifed by the Treaty of Washington, sometimes called the Cession Treaty, which dealt with the islands of Sibutu and Cagayan.

swap.leadin: This legislation was first successfully used in the Supreme Court case United States v. E.C. Knight Company.
swap.text: Name this act passed under President Benjamin Harrison, which was proposed by an Ohio Senator. It was later reinforced and clarified by an act named after Henry De Lamar Clayton.
swap.clue: This act was inspired by a similar act from its namesake senator's home state named for Valentine.

question.text: The Homestead steel works had been bought by this Scottish steel magnate who also wrote "The Gospel of Wealth" and founded a university in Pittsburgh.
question.clue: In 1892 this man's employee Henry Clay Frick hired Pinkerton agents to crush the Homestead Strike.

swap.leadin: This man commissioned Eadweard Muybridge to research the galloping of his horses.
swap.text: Name this member of the "Big Four" who served as president of Southern and Central Pacific during the 1890s and founded a university which he named for his deceased son.
swap.clue: In 1861, this man allied with Charles Huntington, Charles Crocker, and Mark Hopkins to create the Central Pacific Railroad, which met the Union Pacific at Promontory point.

question.leadin: Identify the following about the almost-war between the United States and Great Britain in the 1850s.
question.text: In Central America, the British frequently got into skirmishes with Accessory Transit Company, a firm owned by this shipping tycoon who founded a namesake Southern university.
question.clue: During the California Gold Rush, this person created the Accessory Transit Company to bring passengers from the East Coast to San Francisco via Nicaragua.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the free silver movement per part.
swap.text: This 1878 act rectified the "Crime of 73" by resuming recognition of the silver dollar and requiring at least two million dollars of silver to be coined each month.
swap.clue: It replaced the "Crime of 1873" and mandated a 16-to-1 ratio after it was passed over the veto of Rutherford B. Hayes, who only complied with the minimum requirements of this law.

question.text: One of the few lasting achievements of the Arthur administration was this 1883 bill, attempting to end the office-dealing which led to 's assassination, which mandated merit-based federal employment.
question.clue: This 1883 act guaranteed that citizens could compete for federal appointment on the basis of examinations as opposed to the spoils system.

swap.text: This man repeatedly made the dubious claim that he completed a grueling 322-mile marathon run while working for the Pony Express. Annie Oakley worked as a sharpshooter on a traveling show run by this man.
swap.answerHtml: Buffalo Bill [or Buffalo Bill Cody or William Frederick Cody]
swap.clue: After killing and scalping a Cheyenne warrior named Yellow Hair at Warbonnet Creek, this man shouted, "The first scalp for Custer!"

question.leadin: This man brought to light the harsh treatment of miners in Spring Valley, Illinois, but his writings were unable to prevent a large race riot by anarchist Italian miners.
question.text: Name this author of the 1894 expose Wealth Against Commonwealth, in which he criticizes the business practices of monopolies, most notably Standard Oil.

swap.text: The National Equal Rights Party in 1872 nominated this first woman to run for president, even though she did not meet the constitutional age requirement. Frederick Douglass was unknowingly put on a ticket with this woman.
swap.clue: (+) Although he never acknowledged the decision, Frederick Douglass was selected by this person to be their running mate on the Equal Rights Party ticket during the 1872 election.

question.text: Shocking stories of adultery in this family surrounded a 1934 custody dispute between Gloria Morgan and Gertrude Whitney over possession of a trust fund after the death of Reginald, the son of Cornelius.
question.clue: In 1877, a member of this family paid Woodhull $1,000 to leave the country. A railroad tycoon from this family names a university in Nashville.

swap.leadin: The origin of this organization's name may refer to their leader cross-dressing to pose as an old woman looking for charity.
swap.text: Name this organization that allegedly perpetrated a series of 1870s murders in one state's anthracite regions, resulting in 10 members of this organization being hanged.
swap.clue: This group of Irish coal miners who led a terroristic campaign against mine owners in Pennsylvania and West Virginia in the 1870s.

question.text: Conkling met with James Garfield, pledging to work together and deliver New York to the Republicans, in a treaty informally named for this location. Garfield's violation of this treaty led to Conkling's resignation.

swap.text: The Toronto Women's Literary Club worked with the Ontario branch of this organization to achieve women's suffrage. Annie Turner Wittenmyer first led this originally-American organization, which had the slogan "Do Everything."
swap.clue: Matilda Carse published a predecessor to this organization's newspaper, The Union Signal.

question.leadin: Name the following about the dastardliest of all tariffs, the Wilson-Gorman Tariff.
question.text: Grover Cleveland signed the Wilson-Gorman Tariff into law despite the insidious alterations that Gorman allowed this monopoly to make to the House version of the bill. A particularly biting Harper's Weekly cartoon shows Cleveland shackled behind a cart with this company's name on it, driven by Gorman.
question.answerHtml: the Sugar Trust [accept American Sugar Refining Company; prompt on Sugar]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about free love and the appropriately named Fanny Wright, FTPE.
swap.text: One of the biggest blows to the free love movement was the 1873 passage of this act, which banned the distribution of sexually-oriented publications in the U.S. and declared contraceptives themselves.
swap.clue: Griswold overruled Connecticut's "Little" version of this 1873 Federal law, which made it illegal to distribute "obscene" information, including information on birth control, through the mail.
